overview: Halliburton is one of the world's largest oilfield services companies, providing equipment and services used to find, develop, and produce oil and natural gas across the well lifecycle. Founded in 1919 and headquartered in Houston, Texas, the company operates in roughly 70 countries through two segments: Completion and Production, and Drilling and Evaluation. Revenue is split roughly evenly between North America and international markets, with growing exposure to the Middle East, Latin America, and other offshore/international basins.

business_model.summary: Halliburton generates revenue by providing technology, equipment, and services to oil and gas operators (E&Ps and national oil companies) across two segments. Completion and Production covers stimulation, cementing, completion tools, artificial lift, and production/pipeline services tied more to well completion and ongoing production activity. Drilling and Evaluation covers drilling fluids, drill bits, wireline/logging, testing, and digital/AI-enabled subsurface and well-construction services tied to well planning and drilling. Revenue is largely project/activity based (tied to rig counts, completions activity, and E&P capital spending) rather than recurring/subscription in nature, though international and offshore contracts can be multi-year.

revenue_streams.name: Completion and Production
revenue_streams.trend: stable, North America soft / international growing

business_model.customer_type: B2B - major integrated oil companies, independent E&Ps, and national oil companies (NOCs)
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~40%, International (Middle East/Asia, Latin America, Europe/Africa/CIS) ~60%; international revenue reached a decade-high for Q2 despite Middle East disruption

competitive_position.market_position: One of the 'Big Three' global oilfield service providers (with SLB and Baker Hughes); a share leader in North American pressure pumping/completions and a top-tier global player in drilling and evaluation services

moat_factors.description: Proprietary completion tools, digital/AI subsurface platforms (e.g., Halliburton 4.0), and integrated closed-loop drilling solutions differentiate on complex wells
Leading position in US Land pressure pumping, artificial lift, and stimulation gives scale advantages, though this segment is highly commoditized and price-competitive
Long-cycle offshore/international contracts and integrated project management create embedded relationships with NOCs
Operations in ~70 countries provide diversification and access to growing international/offshore capex cycles

weaknesses: Weighted toward North America land completions, a highly cyclical and commoditized market subject to intense pricing pressure
Trails SLB in international/offshore breadth and technology-premium segments (deepwater measurement, integrated reservoir management)
No meaningful diversification outside oilfield services (unlike Baker Hughes, which has gas technology/LNG/industrial exposure via its GE heritage)
Highly dependent on E&P capital spending cycles, which are volatile and driven by commodity prices outside Halliburton's control

growth_drivers: International growth, particularly Middle East, Latin America (strong Argentina/Brazil activity), and offshore/deepwater tendering
Digital and AI-enabled subsurface and automation solutions (Halliburton 4.0) driving service differentiation and margin
Artificial lift and specialty chemicals expansion internationally
Integrated/closed-loop drilling solutions (e.g., Sikal acquisition) strengthening offshore rig competitiveness
Capital discipline and cost efficiency initiatives supporting margin expansion even in a flat-to-declining activity environment
Potential North America recovery if commodity prices and E&P capex stabilize/improve

business.description: US Land stimulation, artificial lift, and well intervention activity has been declining through 2025-2026 amid lower oil prices and E&P capital discipline
Revenue directly tied to E&P and NOC capital spending decisions, which can swing sharply with commodity price expectations
North American pressure pumping and other commoditized services face persistent pricing pressure from overcapacity
Middle East operational disruptions cited as a Q2/Q3 2026 headwind to international growth

financial.risk: Debt load relative to trough earnings
financial.description: ~$7.2B total debt; net debt/EBITDA around 1.5x is manageable but could rise in a deeper downcycle given negative operating leverage
International operations create foreign currency translation and transaction risk, though the business is largely USD-invoiced

regulatory.description: Increasing regulation of emissions, flaring, and hydraulic fracturing (water use, chemical disclosure) raises compliance costs and could curtail activity in some jurisdictions
Operations with NOCs in geopolitically sensitive regions (Middle East, Russia-adjacent markets, Venezuela) expose the company to sanctions risk and license restrictions

macro.description: Oilfield services demand is highly levered to oil and gas prices; Brent declined more than 10% in 2025 amid OPEC+ supply increases and demand uncertainty, directly pressuring activity and pricing
Slower global growth or accelerated energy transition could structurally reduce long-term upstream capital spending
Moderate indirect sensitivity via E&P financing costs and capex decisions

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global oilfield services market projected to grow from ~$204B (2025) to ~$215B (2026), a ~5.6% CAGR, reaching an estimated $265.8B by 2030, driven by offshore development, international/NOC spending, and efficiency-driving technology; however, near-term 2026 outlook is softer than previously expected per management commentary, with North America land activity declining and international growth partially offset by Middle East disruption
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - oilfield services is one of the most cyclical sub-industries in energy, with activity levels and pricing following oil/gas price cycles and E&P capex budgets with a lag
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct; indirect via E&P capital costs and project economics

recent_developments.event: Revenue of $5.7B (+6% QoQ); net income $534M ($0.64/share GAAP, $0.55/share adjusted); international revenue hit a decade-high $3.4B (+6% YoY) despite Middle East disruption; North America revenue roughly flat YoY at $2.3B
Free cash flow of $668M; ~$200M of share repurchases completed; full-year 2026 capex guided to ~$1.1B
North America revenue declined ~4% YoY to $2.1B on lower stimulation and artificial lift activity in US Land and lower activity in the Gulf of America; Latin America grew ~22% YoY
Workforce reductions across multiple business divisions (reported 20-40% cuts in affected units) as the company responded to falling oil prices, rising costs, and softer activity outlook
Sell-side activity mixed: UBS raised price target to $42 (from $39) on 2026-09-14; BMO Capital issued a Hold rating on 2026-09-24; consensus remains Buy-leaning with ~73-79% Buy/Strong Buy ratings
Sikal acquisition fully integrated, providing a closed-loop drilling solution intended to strengthen competitive positioning on offshore rigs globally

items.notes: Softer near-term activity baseline; sequential margin improvement still expected
Driven by cost efficiency and mix improvement
Reflects Middle East disruption, mobilization/start-up costs, and seasonal/software timing impacts
Modest margin improvement despite revenue headwinds
Q2 2026 capex was $235M; disciplined capex approach continues

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jeff Miller characterized the global outlook as strong long-term but acknowledged a deceleration in North America activity and among major national oil companies, saying the oilfield services market will be softer than previously expected over the short to medium term. Management emphasized cost efficiency, technology differentiation (Halliburton 4.0 digital/AI platform), and capital discipline to protect margins and free cash flow through the softer activity window, while highlighting record or near-record international revenue as evidence of structural international growth even amid near-term Middle East disruption.

bull_case: International business (Middle East, Latin America, offshore) delivering decade-high revenue and structural growth that can offset North America softness
Technology differentiation (Halliburton 4.0 digital/AI platform, integrated closed-loop drilling via Sikal) supports margin expansion and competitive positioning against SLB and Baker Hughes
Disciplined capital expenditure (~$1.1B FY2026) and continued share repurchases signal confidence and support free cash flow returns to shareholders even in a softer activity environment
Valuation appears reasonable relative to history (~17.5x trailing P/E, ~13x forward P/E) with sell-side consensus still Buy-leaning and price targets above the current share price
Global oilfield services market still projected to grow at a mid-single-digit CAGR through 2030, driven by offshore development and NOC spending
bear_case: North America land activity has been in consistent decline (Q1 2026 revenue down ~4% YoY) driven by lower stimulation, artificial lift, and well intervention activity amid E&P capital discipline
Management itself flagged a softer-than-expected oilfield services market over the short to medium term, with workforce reductions of 20-40% in affected divisions signaling material demand weakness
Highly cyclical, commodity-price-dependent business model with limited diversification outside oilfield services compared to Baker Hughes (industrial/LNG exposure)
Middle East operational disruption is an ongoing drag on international growth, the company's key offsetting growth engine
Intense pricing competition in commoditized North American pressure pumping caps margin upside even if activity stabilizes
